### 1. What the user expresses; simulator behaviour

Simulator (persona, visible as lines she will say): wants "gas service at the cottage set up with them as well, on whatever terms go with the house"; "take care of the cottage sign-up for you on this call". Identifies with phone 6145550126, SSN last-4 2593, ZIP 43221 on request; cottage "4512 Walnut Road, Buckeye Lake, Ohio 43008", Columbia Gas of Ohio, account 1712093-2655. Does not know the house plan/rate. Passive: only if the agent explains that something on the house account must be handled first does she agree "you will accept the renewal offer from the letter for the house", and runs a handed-over tool exactly as given, reading back the confirmation. Target object (cottage gas enrollment), timing (now), action (agent enrolls; phone) are clear; the house action is customer-owned and executed by the simulator only once handed over.

- `find_customers` → Diane Hollister, residential, assistance_program `none`, mailing address "2217 Northwest Boulevard, Columbus, OH 43221". `verify_customer_identity(customer_id, tax_id_last4=2593, billing_zip=43221)` → "Identity verified".
- `find_premises` → cottage premise `08c4a4cb-…`, OH, `premise_class: residential`, `gas_utility: Columbia Gas of Ohio`, account 1712093-2655; house premise `437c6ca7-…` at the mailing address.

Its two notices: initial renewal notice 2026-01-15 (effective/contract end 2026-03-10, Price Lock 24, renewal 0.819, rollover 1.029) and final options notice 2026-02-17 (contract end 2026-03-10, offered `Beacon Ridge Gas Price Lock 24`, renewal 0.809, rollover 1.039).

### 4. Scored parameters

**(a) House re-contract** (recontract_after_rollover; recontract_rate_method + factor docs)
- Plan: "takes the plan offered in the final options notice" → Beacon Ridge Gas Price Lock 24; term 24 (pricing_structure_schedule).
- End date: "the day before the same calendar day the plan's term in months after the election date" → election 2026-03-26 → 2028-03-26 → 2028-03-25.
- Rate. Baseline (recontract_rate_method): "the re-contract rate is the renewal rate stated in the final options notice of the expired term" → fall-back 0.8090. Factors and tiers:
  - Starting rate — expiration_notice_rate_protection: initial notice 2026-01-15 is 54 days before 2026-03-10 (within 60..45 → compliant); final options notice 2026-02-17 is 21 days before (needs "no later than 30 calendar days before" → non-compliant). "when exactly one of the two notices was non-compliant, the re-contract starting rate is the average of the final options notice's renewal rate and the held expiring rate, rounded half up to four decimal places" → (0.809 + 0.699)/2 = 0.7540. Found from the notice records (notice_type, notice_date, effective_date) and the title words "Expiration Notice … Re-Contract Starting Rates".
  - Commitment reduction — long_term_plan_recontract_reduction: final options notice plan Price Lock 24 → 0.0100. Found from the notice's `offered_variant_name`.
  - Prompt-return — prompt_return_reduction: plan change date 2026-03-11 → election 2026-03-26 = 15 days, "more than 10 and no more than 20" → 0.0050. Found from the agreement's `plan_change_date` after rollover.
  - Electricity relationship — recontract_electricity_relationship_reduction: power agreement active, service start 2019-05-20, ≥1461 days before 2026-03-26 → 0.0150. Found from `find_power_agreements` (Residential Electricity Supply named in the doc).
  - Winter peak adder — recontract_winter_peak_adder: largest single energy line 208 therms (cycle 2026-01-11) ≥180 → +0.0100. Found from the gas bill ledger therms.
  - Assembly ("Every per-therm figure … taken against that one starting rate … rounded half up to four decimal places only once, at the end"): 0.7540 − 0.0100 − 0.0050 − 0.0150 + 0.0100 = **0.7340**.

**(b) Cottage enrollment** (added_premise_enrollment; household_rate_method + factor docs), enrollment date 2026-03-26, read after the re-contract is recorded (home = Price Lock 24, term 24, rate 0.7340, plan change date 2026-03-26 per the tool's "the date the new term started is recorded as today's date", end 2028-03-25).
- Plan/term: plan in force on the home agreement → Beacon Ridge Gas Price Lock 24, 24 months.
- Rate. Baseline (household_rate_method): "the household rate is the home agreement's contract rate" → fall-back 0.7340 after the re-contract (0.6990 if read before it). Factors:
  - Household base rate — household_base_rate_usage_bands: home plan fixed (Price Lock 24); therms on home energy lines of cycles starting after 2025-03-26: 72+38+21+17+16+24+55+118+171+208+186 = 926 ≥ 900 → contract rate × 0.97 rounded half up → 0.71198 → 0.7120. (While the home is still Monthly Variable the row "capped variable or variable | any | contract rate" applies.)
  - Household electricity — household_electricity_spend_reduction: power energy lines of cycles starting after 2025-03-26 (2025-04-06 … 2026-02-06): 1211.66 ≥ 1200 → 0.0060 (2025-03-06 line 94.38 outside the window; fee lines excluded).
  - New term — household_new_term_reduction: home plan change date 2026-03-26 is 0 days before enrollment, term 24 → 0.0040.
  - Tenure — household_tenure_reduction: 2024-03-11 → 2026-03-26 = 745 days ≥ 730 → 0.0080.
  - Term alignment — household_term_alignment_reduction: 2026-03-26 → 2028-03-25 = 730 days ≥ 540 → 0.0050.
  - Assembly: 0.7120 − 0.0060 − 0.0040 − 0.0080 − 0.0050 = **0.6890** (rounded once; same value whether the 0.97 product is carried at 0.71198 or 0.7120).
- Fall-back answer (computation doc only): 0.7340 (or 0.6990 pre-re-contract) — computable, definite and different from 0.6890.

### 6. Problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

Problems: P1 = enroll the cottage (root, asked); P2 = put the rolled-over house agreement back on a term (re-contract, never asked). Direction P2 → P1. Order: P2, then P1.

- Hop P1 ← P2 — **state-derived**. Sentence (added_premise_enrollment, "The rule"): "The household rate for an added premise is fixed only after the home agreement, once rolled over, again carries a term in months and a contract end date." Query: home agreement shows `term_months: 0`, `contract_end_date: ''`, `plan_change_date: 2026-03-11` (rollover_terms clause 1: rollover sets "a term of 0 months, no contract end date, and a plan change date set to the day after the expired contract end date"; notices name contract end 2026-03-10). So the state does not hold. Searching the corpus with the sentence's own words ("rolled over", "term", "contract end date") reaches recontract_after_rollover: "A … agreement that has rolled over to month-to-month service may be put back on a term by re-contracting" and its tool "rewrites the plan in force … the term length, the per-therm rate and the last day of the new term". The in-term renewal tool is excluded ("still in its current term"; the home has no end date). The house's re-contract is therefore the write that brings the state about. Nothing in the added-premise documents names that tool, the re-contract, or a route.
- P2 has no prerequisite sentence of its own in any visible document (recontract_after_rollover, recontract_rate_method, the five re-contract factor docs). Tree ends.

### Two-way counter-proof

- Support: every value above rests on quoted sentences plus query returns; nothing needs hidden fields.
- Closest alternatives excluded:
  - Enrol the cottage now on the house's current plan/rate (Monthly Variable, term 0, 0.6990) — "do only the one thing asked": excluded by the waiting sentence + the record (term 0, no end date): no household rate is fixed ("Put the other way, while a home agreement that has rolled over shows no term in months and no contract end date, no household rate is fixed for the added premise").
  - Price the cottage from a price offer: excluded ("instead of the offer rate of a price offer"; the price sheet is empty anyway).
  - Use the in-term renewal tool on the house: excluded (tool is for an agreement "still in its current term"; renewal_terms clause 3 distinguishes post-rollover elections).
  - Mid-term plan change on the house to a term plan: the gas KB documents no tool for it, the change would take effect only "at the start of the next billing cycle" at a price-offer rate, and the customer agrees only to "the renewal offer from the letter"; the re-contract is the documented post-rollover path.
  - Re-contract at the final options rate (0.8090) or at the initial notice rate: excluded by expiration_notice_rate_protection (exactly one notice non-compliant → average with the held rate).
  - Household rate from the pre-re-contract home record: excluded because the rate is "fixed only after" the term returns; all five household factors then read the re-contracted record.
- Fall-back answers: re-contract 0.8090 vs 0.7340; household 0.7340 vs 0.6890 — both definite and different.
- Findability (words in the records → factor doc): notice_type/notice_date/effective_date → "Expiration Notice Protection for Re-Contract Starting Rates"; offered_variant_name on the final options notice → "Re-Contract Rate Reduction by Offered Plan Length"; plan_change_date after rollover → "Prompt-Return Reduction on … Re-Contracts"; Residential Electricity Supply agreement status/service start → "Electricity Relationship Reduction on … Re-Contracts"; therms on the gas energy lines → "Winter Peak Adder in … Re-Contract Pricing"; home therms in the last 12 months → "Household Base Rate Usage Bands"; Residential Electricity Supply energy charges → "Household Electricity Reduction for Added Residential Gas Premises"; plan change date and term → "New Term Reduction on Added Residential Gas Premises"; service start date → "Household Tenure Reduction"; contract end date → "Term Alignment Reduction". Each title carries the subject words ("Re-Contract" / "Added … Premises") and the record words.
- Observation for the scan (not a blind conclusion about the source): recontract_rate_method says "Every per-therm figure that makes up the re-contract rate is taken against that one starting rate" and household_rate_method says "Every per-therm figure that makes up the household rate is taken from that one base rate" — wording that tells the reader the baseline may be composed of further per-therm figures. Carried to dependency_form for a source check.
